newsitem.title: USA: Rain seen further hampering Illinois barge traffic.
newsitem.headline: Rain seen further hampering Illinois barge traffic.

text.p: Heavy rains moving into central Illinois on Wednesday could snag already slow barge traffic on the lower portion of the Illinois River, experts said.

"It is raining at Starved Rock Lock (near Utica, Ill.,) down to LaGrange Lock," said Rick Granados, chief of Lock and Dam Section for the Illinois Waterway Project, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. "But if the river levels reach the heights of the levies down there, then barge traffic could slow down."
On Tuesday, the Coast Guard issued wake speed restrictions for tows between LaSalle, Ill., and Grafton, Ill., Granados said.
Granados added that all locks which were closed to navigation due to rising waters from heavy rains late last week were now back in operation.

Starved Rock Lock opened on Tuesday while Marseilles Lock at Marseilles, Ill., and Dresden Island Lock, near Morris, Ill., were open on Monday. "But there is still a width restriction at Dresden Island Lock," Granados said.

Meteorologists said central Illinois can expect up to two inches of rain in the next 24 to 36 hours which could trigger a renewed rise in river levels or a slowing of the recession of water from previous rainfall.

"From Wednesday morning to Thursday morning it looks like the lower Illinois River basin and the middle Illinois River basin have a forecast of an average of two inches of rain over it," said Ray Kopsky, hydraulic engineer with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, St Louis District.
And the Illinois River was still rising below Peoria. The crest was nearing Havana, Ill., said Bill Morris, hydrologist at the National Weather Service in Chicago.
Morris said there was a potential for renewed rising of water on many tributaries feeding into the Illinois River.
